security_audit.summary: The real risks are the documented uv/python execution path and repeated access to a hidden ~/.claude directory. Most markdown backtick detections are false positives, but the hidden-path script target and unpinned runtime dependencies need remediation before broad publishing.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the hardcoded ~/.claude path and invoke a bundled script through a verified skill runtime path.
Include extract_chapters.py in the submitted package or remove commands that reference it.
Pin dependency versions and provide a lockfile or equivalent reviewed dependency metadata.
Validate EPUB and output paths before execution and document safe handling for paths with spaces or special characters.

semantic_findings.title: Unverifiable Local Script Execution

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Dependency Installation

content.value_statement: Long EPUB files are hard to review when every chapter stays inside one ebook container. This skill documents a workflow that extracts chapters into numbered Markdown files for editing and analysis.
actual_capabilities: Provides a uv command pattern for running an EPUB chapter extraction script.
Supports an optional output directory argument in the documented workflow.
Documents default output folder behavior when no output directory is provided.
Shows numbered Markdown filenames for predictable chapter sorting.
Describes the expected chapter Markdown format with a title and body content.
limitations: The referenced extract_chapters.py script is not included in the scanned source.
The commands assume uv, Python, and runtime package installation are available.
The workflow does not document image, table, or stylesheet preservation.
The hardcoded ~/.claude skill path may not match every tool or installation.

use_cases.description: Split a manuscript EPUB into chapter files that can be reviewed in a Markdown editor.

use_cases.title: Create Documentation Source Files
use_cases.description: Turn an ebook-style source file into ordered Markdown chapters for documentation workflows.

output_examples.input: Extract chapters from a history EPUB using the default folder.
output_examples.output: Created a folder next to the EPUB with numbered Markdown chapter files. The files are ready for review in chapter order.

output_examples.input: Extract an EPUB into a custom editorial draft folder.
output_examples.output: Placed the extracted chapter Markdown files in the requested folder and reported the generated chapter count.

output_examples.input: Check the extracted chapter files after conversion.
output_examples.output: Reported the output folder, listed the generated chapter filenames, and noted any chapters that need manual review.

best_practices: Run the workflow only on EPUB files from trusted sources.
Choose a clear output folder before extraction to avoid mixing chapter files.
Review generated Markdown for missing images, tables, or unusual formatting.
anti_patterns: Do not run the command when the referenced extractor script is missing or unreviewed.
Do not overwrite an existing chapter folder without checking its contents first.
Do not assume every EPUB navigation structure maps cleanly to chapters.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It documents a workflow for extracting EPUB chapters into separate numbered Markdown files.

faq.question: What tools does it require?
faq.answer: It expects uv, Python, and the Python packages listed in the command to be available at runtime.

faq.question: Where are the Markdown files written?
faq.answer: If no output folder is provided, the workflow creates a folder beside the EPUB file.

faq.question: Can I choose a custom output folder?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented command accepts an optional output directory argument.

faq.question: Does it preserve images and formatting?
faq.answer: The skill only documents chapter text extraction into Markdown. It does not promise full EPUB formatting preservation.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The audit found hidden-path command execution and unpinned runtime dependencies that require review before use.
